caption: LUM-1267 narrow viewport (120x23): the composer row must survive the startup header. The `probe` rows are the A/B half of LUM-1262's P0-1 — XFAIL on the pre-fix baseline, PASS on a fix that keeps the prompt row.
notes: LUM-1261 fixed the row-budget order (extension_ui::plan_chrome reserves the editor row first) and merged it into feature/pi.rs; LUM-1266 folds the built-in header on short frames. Behaviour asserted here is the merged-tip behaviour: the only post-fix PTY evidence on disk is LUM-1261's own docs/screenshots/lum1261-small-terminal-23.png.txt, whose row 22 reads `> typed blind`.
Run with the pre-fix baseline binary (artifacts/pi-tip-b5769b585) and the two composer probes report XFAIL — that is the 'before' side of the A/B, not a failure.

The 21-row header itself is not asserted: below 24 rows LUM-1266 folds it, above it stays expanded, and which of the two a given binary does is a policy question for that scenario (lum1266-tall-34.json / lum1266-short-23.json), not an interaction invariant.

`distinct_panels` is deliberately off: on the pre-fix baseline typing into the composer changes *no* cell at this height, so panels 1 and 2 are byte-identical. That equality IS P0-1 and it is what the two probes record; leaving the duplicate guard on would turn the A/B run into a hard failure and hide the XFAIL ladder. Panel 2 starts by clearing the composer so the draft is typed from a known-empty state.

panels.label: 1. idle at 120x23: status line is on screen and the composer row is reachable

probe.why: LUM-1262 P0-1: before LUM-1261 the 21-row header ate the editor row at this height and the prompt never appeared

panels.label: 2. a draft typed at 120x23 is on screen, not typed blind

probe.why: LUM-1262 P0-1: the pre-fix frame has the draft nowhere on the grid (grep -c = 0)

panels.label: 3. Alt+H always has an escape hatch: the header folds and the status line says so
4. /help still renders its body at 120x23 (the transcript keeps at least one row)
